evals.prompt: Review PR #212 on this repo (checked out on branch pr-212). The author's description says 'refactor only, no behavior change'. Is that true?
evals.expected_output: Writes the behavioral summary from the diff BEFORE reading the author's description, then diffs the two — any undisclosed behavior change is a headline finding; follows untouched callers from blast radius into the code; report lands at docs/pr-212.html with a verdict-led summary; the caveat on the name-based blast radius travels into the walkthrough; docs/codemap.html is left untouched — atlas refreshes are not part of a PR review.

evals.prompt: quick sanity check on my uncommitted changes before i push? i'm on main. some of the files are brand new
evals.expected_output: Uses --worktree (which must include the untracked new files and fall back to HEAD as base on a mainline checkout); produces a proportionate report — a small diff gets a short report, empty fragments dropped rather than padded; if a coverage artifact exists, the changed files' measured coverage appears with its age caveat.

evals.prompt: what does this branch change vs main? it's mostly a big file rename/move plus a couple of small edits. is it safe to merge?
evals.expected_output: Renames are surfaced with old→new paths, and the report says what rename-safety the tooling can NOT check (stale path-based references, imports) instead of calling silence proof of safety; the verdict distinguishes the mechanical move from the behavioral edits; no heuristic miss is presented as evidence of absence.
